name: 从句深度分析
description: Measures the nesting depth of clauses within sentences to detect AI-generated text's tendency toward shallow embedding structures.
useCase: Detecting AI text through uniform and shallow subordinate clause patterns
mechanism: Parses sentences into clause hierarchies and measures embedding depth (main clause → subordinate clause → embedded clause). Computes maximum depth, mean depth, depth variance, and depth distribution per sentence. AI-generated text typically shows lower maximum clause depth and less variation in depth across sentences, reflecting a flatter information packaging strategy compared to human writers who naturally vary between simple and deeply embedded constructions.
source: Hunt, K. W. (1965) - Grammatical Structures Written at Three Grade Levels, NCTE Research Report
algorithm: Clause Boundary Detection + Depth Calculation + Statistical Distribution Analysis
parameters: Parser: dependency-based clause segmenter, Depth metrics: max/mean/variance/distribution, Sentence min: 5 words, Text min: 10 sentences
strengths:
• Captures information packaging complexity
• Linguistically well-motivated feature
• Complementary to sentence-level metrics
• Effective on formal and academic writing
limitations:
• Parser-dependent accuracy
• Some genres favor simple clause structures naturally
• Modern LLMs can produce complex embeddings
• Requires reliable clause boundary detection

references.title: Hunt, K. W. (1965). Grammatical Structures Written at Three Grade Levels. NCTE Research Report No. 3.
Gibson, E. (1998). Linguistic Complexity: Locality of Syntactic Dependencies. Cognition.
Tang, R. et al. (2023). The Science of Detecting LLMs-Generated Text. arXiv.
